ev.q: During January-October 1998, 123 of 160 doses of penicillin administered for syphilis were Bicillin C-R.
After 8 weeks of follow-up efforts, 52 (82%) of the 63 patients had been restaged and retreated
31 (56%) were unaware of the possible confusion between Bicillin C-R and Bicillin L-A
Besides the Maryland clinics, four program areas reported unintentional Bicillin C-R use at least once from 1993 through 1998.
Sixty-three patients, including five pregnant women, might have received Bicillin C-R.
55 (96%) of the state/city program areas responded to the survey.
The total estimated direct costs of follow-up efforts conducted by county A's clinic was approximately $24,000.

public_health_question.v: How many syphilis patients in a Maryland county STD clinic were inadequately treated with Bicillin C-R, what follow-up was required, and how often has such inadvertent use occurred in STD programs nationwide?

equity.level_reason: No social-position dimension is reported or discussed; patients are described only by pregnancy and treatment status.

notes: A medication-error field investigation in two Maryland county clinics combined with a CDC survey of STD program areas; all results are counts and percentages with no comparisons or inference. The $24,000 follow-up cost is a single descriptive estimate, not a cost analysis.
view_issues: '24 (46%) program areas routinely ordered Bicillin L-A by telephone' is inconsistent with the denominator of 55 (24/55 = 44%).
